steps.title: The Earth and Sun
steps.say: Many people think seasons are caused by Earth getting closer to or farther from the Sun, but that is a myth.

steps.title: Earth's Axial Tilt
steps.say: The real cause is Earth's axial tilt of 23.5 degrees, which always points in the same direction in space as we orbit the Sun.

steps.title: Northern Winter
steps.say: In December, the Northern Hemisphere tilts away from the Sun, receiving indirect light and shorter days, creating winter.

steps.title: Northern Summer
steps.say: Six months later in June, the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, getting direct sunlight and long days, which brings summer.

steps.title: Equinoxes
steps.say: During spring and autumn, neither hemisphere tilts toward or away from the Sun, so both receive equal amounts of daylight.

steps.title: Check Your Understanding
steps.say: Can you drag the Earth along its orbit to find where it is summer in the Southern Hemisphere?

steps.title: Explore the Orbit
steps.say: Great job! Try dragging Earth to any point on its orbit to see how sunlight angles and day lengths change throughout the year.
